data.body:
## FIXED-738A-B: implemented per the operator's ruling — Gerrit 1378, verified end-to-end

Ruling: *update the close gate to provide attestation for duplicates with a live link.* Done.

### Shape of the fix

A disposition close now returns a **sign signal** instead of `None`, so the existing signing path
mints the op-cert with no special-casing at the call site. It is **deterministic — no LLM call**,
because there is still nothing to verify; the exemption's original justification is untouched.

**The manifest does not claim a completion PASS.** That was the design constraint I would not trade
away: a signature reading `completion-verifier: PASS` for a ticket whose completion was never
verified is a lie in the signed bytes, and an auditor could no longer distinguish a verified
completion from a bookkeeping disposition. What 0059 now actually carries:

```
completion-verifier: DISPOSITION duplicate
replacement: 23ed-de0a-765b-49aa
ticket: 0059-c7f0-cce1-4077
model: none (deterministic disposition)
runner: close_disposition
rebar-version: 0.10.1
material: 48469f827ce62b75
```

`kind` is derived as the text before the first `": "` (`reducer/_processors_identity.py`), so this is
still a `completion-verifier` record and `verify_signature(kind="completion-verifier")` finds it. The
`material:` step is preserved, so validity-on-read still invalidates it after a post-verdict edit —
identical semantics to a verified completion, not a permanently-valid special case.

### Verified END TO END, not just in units

```
verify_signature(0059, kind="completion-verifier")  ->  certified
child_closure_findings(e369)  ->  uncertified 2 -> 1   (only b586 remains)
```

### All three exempt classes, because two were LATENT

Measured before the fix: only `duplicate` had closes carrying a live link (7 of them, all unsigned).
`not_a_bug` had **zero** linked closes and `escalated` had **zero closed bugs at all** — so both sat
on the identical code path and would have produced the identical gap the first time one was linked.
The fix keys on the same class-set + link predicate, so they are covered before that happens rather
than after. The remaining no-code-change classes (`flaky`, `env_integration`, `undetermined`,
`preexisting`) are NOT dispositions: they still run the verifier and were already being certified, so
widening the set to them would have removed real verification.

### `--force-close` still withholds the signature, and that is now pinned

Its guard runs BEFORE the disposition branch, so a `--force-close --class duplicate` on a linked bug
produces no sign signal. That ordering is load-bearing now in a way it was not before — if reversed,
the operator's escape hatch would become a way to certify without verifying. **Mutation-checked:**
moving the guard after the disposition branch makes the new test fail with exactly that message;
restoring it makes it pass. A guarantee asserted without a demonstrated RED would have been worth
little here.

### Placement

The logic is a new module (`_commands/close_disposition.py`) rather than more lines in
`transition_close.py`, which is at its size ceiling and is being split by another session; the call
site there changes by two lines and `_verdict_manifest` gains a three-line delegation.
